Add monitoring/logging for future investigation\n\n**But:** 95% of \"no root cause\" cases are incomplete investigation.\n\n## Supporting Techniques\n\n---\nname: instrumenting-control-planes\ndescription: Use when building, planning, reviewing, or debugging apps with backend decisions, agent workflows, long-running jobs, SSE/WebSocket streams, recovery paths, deletes, retries, or user-visible failures\n---\n\n# Instrumenting Control Planes\n\nBuild the control plane as a product surface. If the server decides, refuses, retries, spawns, deletes, recovers, gives up, or fails, that decision must be observable by users, operators, and tests.\n\nIf a React UI consumes the control plane through server state, optimistic UI, caches, polling, SSE/WebSocket streams, or persisted runtime state, also use `client-server-state-invariants`.\n\n## Core Rule\n\nEvery meaningful server-side state transition emits a named, durable event. The UI and tests consume the same production event surface.\n\nDo not rely on snapshot diffs, rendered DOM state, logs only, or client-side re-derivation to prove what the server decided.\n\n## Hot Path Rule\n\nNo user bootstrap, catalog, status, reconnect, or recovery request may depend on a lock-prone database write path or external health probe finishing. Serve these paths from a bounded read model, memory cache, append-only event log, or stale-but-marked snapshot; queue reconciliation writes outside the request. Every dependency on a database or bridge call in a hot path needs a short timeout, cancellation, and an explicit degraded response.\n\nIf SQLite, local files, or a single-writer store is used, assume writer contention can freeze readers at the worst moment. Use one writer, WAL/busy-timeout discipline, short transactions, bounded queues, and headless chaos tests that run bootstrap/reload while writes are active. A 25s UI request is a control-plane failure, even if the database eventually returns.\n\n## Event Contract\n\nFor each backend or agent workflow, define:\n\n- named events for decisions: `worker.spawned`, `worker.reattached`, `plan.ready`, `plan.review.blocked`, `recovery.gave_up`, `conversation.delete_failed`;\n- payloads with stable ids, `prev`/`next` status when relevant, reason codes, and enough context to debug;\n- `error.surfaced` or an equivalent user-facing failure event for every failure the user should know about;\n- durable persistence or a bounded replay buffer so short disconnects do not erase history;\n- a scriptable read path: CLI, HTTP endpoint, sqlite query, or event log command.\n\nIf a decision cannot be asserted from this surface, the design is incomplete.\n\nIf debugging a control-plane failure reveals a reusable lesson, use `ultrapowers:learning-from-bugs` after the fix is verified.\n\n## Streaming Requirements\n\nFor SSE or WebSocket-like streams:\n\n- emit named events alongside any snapshot/update frame;\n- include monotonic event ids;\n- support resume from the last seen id;\n- replay missed events from a bounded buffer;\n- emit an explicit resync-required event when replay is impossible;\n- bootstrap from a snapshot, then tail events.\n\nSnapshots show current truth. Named events show why it became true.\n\n## Testing Standard\n\nControl-plane tests should usually be headless HTTP/SSE scenario tests, not browser tests. Browser automation is for UI behavior; control-plane tests assert server decisions directly.\n\nWrite scenario assertions as event transcripts:\n\n```ts\nexpect(events).toHaveEmitted(\"worker.spawned\", { runId });\nexpect(events).toHaveEmitted(\"worker.status\", { next: \"running\" });\nchaos.killServer();\nchaos.restartServer();\nexpect(events).toHaveEmitted(\"worker.reattached\", { runId });\nexpect(events).not.toHaveEmitted(\"worker.recreated\", { runId });\n```\n\nChaos belongs outside production code paths: drop connections in the client, fail fetches in the harness, restart the server process, and use seeds for reproducibility.\n\n## Refuse These Shapes\n\n- silent early returns in server methods;\n- swallowed `catch` blocks;\n- client-side derivation of server decisions;\n- response-code-only user failures;\n- event streams without ids or resume;\n- tests that infer control-plane behavior from rendered state;\n- delete handlers that do not enumerate dependent rows or emit typed failure events;\n- recovery loops without terminal events such as `gave_up` or `abandoned`;\n- request handlers that wait on inline reconciliation writes, SQLite contention, or bridge `/doctor` checks before returning bootstrap data;\n- test-only behavior branches in production code.\n\n## Design Checklist\n\nBefore implementing a backend or agent workflow, answer:\n\n1. What decisions can this workflow make?\n2. What named event is emitted for each decision, including refusal and failure?\n3. Where are events persisted or buffered?\n4. How does a client resume after disconnect?\n5. Which request paths must keep working while persistence or bridge dependencies are slow, locked, or stale?\n6. How can a CLI or test harness inspect the exact event sequence without the UI?\n7. Which headless scenario proves the happy path, failure path, recovery path, terminal state, and hot-path timeout/degraded path?\n8. Which client state consumes these events, and how does it prove ownership, freshness, completeness, ordering, and replay/resync?\n\nIf the answer is \"the UI can figure it out\", name the missing event instead.\n---\nname: client-server-state-invariants\ndescription: Use when planning, building, reviewing, or debugging React apps with server state, optimistic UI, caches, polling, SSE/WebSocket streams, background jobs, persistence, or client/server synchronization\n---\n\n# Client Server State Invariants\n\nReact bugs often expose deeper ownership mistakes. When client state, server state, cache state, stream state, and persisted state all exist, every plan needs explicit invariants.\n\n## Core Rule\n\nNo UI surface may treat data as authoritative unless the payload proves ownership, freshness, completeness, ordering, and terminal state.\n\nIf those words are missing from the plan, the plan is probably baking in a race condition.\n\n## Planning Checklist\n\nFor every React app that reads server/runtime state, the plan must answer:\n\n1. **Owner:** What owns this state: server, client manager, URL, cache, stream, local storage, or worker/runtime?\n2. **Token:** What owner token protects async results: `requestId`, `runId`, `projectPath`, `operationId`, `workerId + seq`, or equivalent?\n3. **Provenance:** Is data server-authoritative, optimistic, cached preview, partial update, or historical fallback?\n4. **Completeness:** Does the payload declare what scope it is complete for? What may it erase?\n5. **Ordering:** What stable order is used: monotonic seq, `(createdAt, id)`, version, or cursor?\n6. **State machine:** What are the legal states, terminal states, and transitions?\n7. **Events:** Which server decisions are named events rather than client-side derivations?\n8. **Loading shape:** Which states are bootstrap, first load, incremental refresh, reconnect, resync, recovery, and terminal error?\n9. **Fallbacks:** Which legacy/fallback rows can render, and only after what authority is loaded?\n10. **Tests:** Which race, stale-response, event-sequence, reconnect, and merge tests prove the invariants?\n\n## Invariants To Require\n\n- Cached and optimistic data may pre-render, but cannot satisfy full-load gates.\n- Partial snapshots may add or refine state, but may not erase optimistic objects, delivered user input, read markers, or stream entries unless they declare complete scope.\n- Every async response checks that its owner token still matches before mutating visible state.\n- Mutation success handlers may navigate or clear UI only if they still own the current context, unless the action explicitly creates a new selected context.\n- Timers and polling callbacks re-check ownership immediately before acting.\n- Server decisions are emitted as named events; the client does not infer decisions by diffing snapshots.\n- SSE/WebSocket streams have event ids, replay/resume, and an explicit resync path.\n- Loading booleans are split by lifecycle stage. A leaf stream refresh must not unmount the whole page.\n- Append-only content has one writer, one reader, stable ids, and monotonic cursors.\n- Fallback DB rows or historical rows are gated behind stream loading and deduped by stable id plus safe equivalence.\n- Status classifiers distinguish active, runnable, blocked, awaiting user, terminal, stale, and recoverable states.\n- \"Latest\" queries have deterministic tie-breakers. Timestamp-only ordering is not enough.\n- Hot paths use bounded reads and do not synchronously load large bodies, bridge probes, schema setup, or heavy app graphs.\n- Process-local caches have explicit TTL/size bounds and invalidation rules.\n\n## Test Matrix\n\nPick the rows that match the work. Do not rely on one happy-path UI test.\n\n| Risk | Test shape |\n| --- | --- |\n| Stale async response | Start request A, switch owner, resolve A, assert it cannot mutate B |\n| Optimistic object erased | Create local optimistic state, apply stale/partial snapshot, assert object remains |\n| Cache masquerades as loaded | Hydrate cache preview, assert full-load gate waits for server authority |\n| Mutation steals navigation | Start mutation, switch selection, resolve mutation, assert focus stays put |\n| Timer/poll stale-fire | Use fake timers or deferred promises; callback must re-check owner before acting |\n| Snapshot merge erases stream | Apply partial snapshot missing known entries, assert entries/read markers remain |\n| Event stream gap | Bootstrap snapshot, emit events during disconnect, reconnect with last id, assert replay or resync |\n| Server decision invisible | Exercise branch and assert named event such as `blocked`, `refused`, `gave_up`, or `error.surfaced` |\n| State classifier wrong | Table-test every status into active/runnable/terminal/recoverable buckets |\n| Fallback duplicates stream | Load fallback rows then stream entries, assert no duplicate or false chronology |\n| Hot path bloats | Assert snapshots carry cursors not bodies; route returns before DB/heavy imports when possible |\n| Timestamp tie | Insert equal timestamps, assert deterministic order by id/seq |\n\nUse headless HTTP/SSE tests for control-plane decisions. Use React/unit tests for manager merging and ownership guards. Use Playwright only for real UI layout, focus, scroll, mobile computed styles, and visible affordances.\n\n## Refuse These Shapes\n\n- one `isLoading` boolean for bootstrap, refresh, reconnect, and recovery;\n- cache or optimistic data treated as authoritative without provenance;\n- async callbacks that mutate state without checking owner tokens;\n- client-side derivation of server decisions;\n- snapshot diffs used as the only way to know what happened;\n- event streams without ids or resume;\n- timestamp-only \"latest\" queries;\n- parallel transcript or persistence surfaces that the frontend must reconcile;\n- unbounded process caches introduced to hide slow storage;\n- tests that prove only the DOM result when the bug is a server decision.\n\n## Review Prompt\n\nAsk this before implementation starts:\n\n> What can arrive late, out of order, partially, twice, or after the user changes context, and what test proves it cannot corrupt visible state?\n---\nname: optimizing-react-next-apps\ndescription: Use when a React or Next.js app feels slow, cluttered, overbundled, slow to compile, slow to load, ineffective at SSR, hydration-heavy, or likely burdened by unnecessary imports or UI dependencies\n---\n\n# Optimizing React And Next Apps\n\nUse this when performance, bundle size, root load time, dev compile time, or UI clutter is the problem. Optimize from evidence, not vibes.\n\n## First Questions\n\nBefore changing code, identify which layer is slow:\n\n- cold dev compile,\n- warm route response,\n- initial HTML usefulness,\n- hydration and client JavaScript,\n- client-side data boot,\n- slow API route,\n- long-lived stream/SSE request being mistaken for slowness.\n\nFor Next.js, SSR being \"on\" is not enough. If the initial HTML does not contain the primary visible UI or data, SSR is only decorative.\n\n## Evidence To Gather\n\n- Dev server logs: compile time, route time, module count.\n- Initial HTML: `curl` the route and check whether meaningful UI text is present.\n- Emitted chunks: inspect `.next/static/chunks/app/*.js` sizes and whether heavy modules are in the root page chunk.\n- Import graph suspects: icon packs, markdown/highlight libraries, charting, code editors, terminal renderers, component suites, popover/dialog stacks, QR/image libraries.\n- Client boot gates: auth/session fetches, settings fetches, route parsing in `useEffect`, query waterfalls, SSE snapshot fetches.\n\n## Default Fixes\n\n- Shrink client boundaries. Do not put the whole page behind one giant `\"use client\"` app shell if a server component can render the first useful screen.\n- Server-bootstrap route-stable data: auth/session, settings needed for shell choice, selected route ids, and initial snapshots. Hydrate Managers or query caches from that data.\n- Lazy-load rarely opened surfaces: settings, onboarding, side windows, file viewers, terminals, workers panels, QR/pairing dialogs, markdown/code viewers.\n- Split tiny shared controls out of heavy feature modules. Never import a whole worker/sidebar/settings surface for one button or toggle.\n- Replace overpowered UI primitives with native controls when the interaction is simple. A basic select should not import a popover/dialog/menu stack.\n- Avoid root/barrel imports from large libraries when subpath imports or local assets are available.\n- Inline tiny stable SVGs instead of adding icon packages. Do not add a package for one logo unless there is a strong reason.\n- Keep browser-only work in effects: localStorage preferences, notifications, focus, SSE/WebSocket startup, post-paint refresh. Do not make `useEffect()` the only route to first meaningful content.\n\n## Next.js-Specific Checks\n\n- In dev, separate first-request compilation from runtime slowness.\n- Check rewrites and catch-all routes: a rewritten URL can still compile and serve the same root page.\n- Watch for client query waterfalls after hydration. React Query is useful, but not a substitute for server bootstrapping when the data gates the first screen.\n- If a route is expected to SSR, verify with `curl` that the expected text is present before hydration.\n- Treat `next/font/google` as a dev/build-time dependency unless local font assets are used.\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n- \"SSR is enabled, so load should be instant\" while the page returns only a client boot shell.\n- Importing a component from a feature module because it happens to export a small helper.\n- Adding icon, syntax, markdown, chart, or UI packages for tiny visual needs.\n- Calling a long SSE request \"slow\" without checking whether it is intentionally open.\n- Optimizing API code when the real cost is compiling a huge client graph.\n- Measuring only warm HMR and claiming cold start is fixed.\n\n## Verification\n\nAfter changes, report before/after evidence:\n\n- root chunk size,\n- module count or trace summary,\n- cold compile time if measured,\n- warm route time,\n- whether heavy modules left the root chunk,\n- typecheck/lint/test results appropriate to the touched surface.\n"
  }

The lesson is blunt: the app must serve the page and control-plane\n> hot paths even while workers, supervisors, bridge polling, and persistence are\n> busy.\n\n## Why This Exists\n\nOn May 20, 2026 the local app repeatedly became unresponsive while a supervisor\nprocess was managing a long-running worker. Chrome showed hard reloads stuck in\n`pending`, and server logs showed request times that are unacceptable for a\ncontrol plane:\n\n```text\nGET /api/events?runId=ca18b7e86437 200 in 55543ms\nGET /api/events?snapshot=1&persisted=1&runId=70a589b48ba5... 200 in 103695ms\nGET /api/workers/70a589b48ba5-worker-2/entries?afterSeq=0 200 in 80421ms\n```\n\nLater live evidence was worse:\n\n```text\nGET /api/events?runId=ca18b7e86437 200 in 487273ms\nGET / 200 in 325220ms\nGET /api/workers/ca18b7e86437-worker-3/entries?afterSeq=250 401 in 62700ms\n```\n\nAnother reload failure exposed the same class of bug through optional catalog\nwork:\n\n```text\nGET /api/agents/catalog 200 in 65581ms\nGET /api/agents/catalog 200 in 122868ms\nGET / 200 in 130440ms\nGET /session/8ad0c5c3f219 200 in 130473ms\n```\n\nThis was not a cosmetic frontend problem. The server was failing the basic\nproduct promise: serve the page, show current state, and keep worker streams\nusable while work is running.\n\n## Symptoms We Observed\n\n- Hard reloads and normal reloads could sit in Chrome's Network tab as\n  `pending` instead of returning the HTML shell.\n- Worker stream polling became slower as workers produced more transcript\n  content.\n- `/api/events` snapshots took tens of seconds to minutes.\n- `/api/agents/catalog` could spend more than a minute on worker/model\n  discovery while the user was only trying to load an existing conversation.\n- The Next dev process repeatedly printed `[db] schema ready`, which was a sign\n  that request/module evaluation was reopening DB-backed modules.\n- A contaminated long-running dev process held dozens of sqlite-related file\n  descriptors. In the live incident, the old Next process held 34 sqlite FDs.\n- The app appeared worse with supervisor-driven worker turns because the\n  supervisor increased worker-history reads, bridge polling, event snapshots,\n  and worker stream traffic.\n\n## Root Causes\n\n### 1. Snapshots Included Worker Transcript Bodies\n\nPersisted event bootstrap and snapshot payloads loaded worker entries directly\nfrom disk and included them in `workerEntries`. That meant a page reload or\n`/api/events?snapshot=1&persisted=1` could walk large worker transcripts before\nresponding.\n\nSnapshots need cursors, not transcript bodies. The worker stream endpoint is\nthe content authority.\n\n### 2. Worker Stream Reads Were Full-File Reads\n\n`GET /api/workers/:workerId/entries?afterSeq=N` could fall back to reading and\nparsing the whole JSONL transcript even when the client only needed entries\nafter a recent cursor. As a worker transcript grew, every poll became more\nexpensive.\n\nIncremental reads must use the JSONL tail for `afterSeq > 0` and only fall\nback to canonical full reads for legacy, compressed, corrupt, or first-load\ncases.\n\n### 3. Worker Stream Writes Rebuilt Caches On Every Append\n\nThe writer assigned seqs and deduplicated bridge entries by rebuilding the\nseen-id/fingerprint state from the full JSONL file on each append. Streaming\nassistant text made this especially bad: each new chunk paid the cost of all\nprevious chunks.\n\nThe normal append path must be O(new entries), not O(transcript history). The\nwriter cache is allowed to rebuild from disk on first use after process start\nor when file stats prove another writer touched the file.\n\n### 4. Hot Routes Imported DB-Backed Modules Too Early\n\nSome unauthenticated or no-cookie paths imported modules that immediately\ncreated DB clients and initialized schema, even though the request could have\nreturned without touching sqlite. This happened on routes like worker entries\nand auth/session bootstrap.\n\nHot-path imports are part of runtime behavior. A top-level import of a DB\nmodule is a DB dependency for every request that loads that route module.\n\n### 5. DB Client State Was Not Stable Across Module Re-Evaluation\n\nNext dev and runtime module re-evaluation can reload server modules. A DB client\ncreated as a plain module singleton is not necessarily a process singleton in\nthat environment. Repeated evaluation created more sqlite clients and handles.\n\nResource singletons in the dev server must be process-scoped and keyed by the\nactual resource path.\n\n### 6. Page SSR Blocked On Too Much Application State\n\nThe root page SSR path built a rich bootstrap payload that could include auth\nstate, settings, and event snapshots. That made \"serve HTML\" depend on the same\nslow paths as \"hydrate full app state\".\n\nThe page must return a shell quickly. Runtime bootstrap, settings, event\nsnapshots, and worker transcripts are client/runtime follow-up requests.\n\n### 7. Root Client Bundle Compilation Could Block HTML In Dev\n\nEven after server bootstrap was narrowed, the root page imported the entire\n`HomeApp` client graph up front. In Next dev, compiling that graph could block\nthe first HTML response for the page, especially while the server was already\nunder load.\n\nThe shell must be small. Heavy app graphs can load behind a dynamic client\nboundary with an immediate boot shell.\n\n### 8. Catalog Discovery Was Treated As Load-Bearing State\n\nThe frontend eagerly requested `/api/agents/catalog` during app bootstrap and\nconversation reloads, even though catalog data is optional metadata for\nonboarding, settings, and explicit refresh. The route could also perform\nblocking local CLI availability probes. When a CLI probe or login shell stalled,\nconversation load stalled behind work that was unrelated to rendering the\nselected transcript.\n\nCatalog discovery must be demand-driven and bounded. Existing conversations can\nrender from persisted run/worker metadata and cached/static worker definitions;\nthey must not wait for fresh worker availability, model discovery, or CLI health\nchecks.\n\n## Fixes That Addressed The Incident\n\n- Persisted snapshots now publish `workerEntrySeqs` instead of `workerEntries`.\n- Snapshot builders use `readWorkerLatestSeq()` rather than\n  `readWorkerEntriesSince(..., 0)` for worker cursor hints.\n- Worker entry reads use a bounded JSONL tail reader for incremental cursors.\n- Worker entry writes keep next-seq, seen ids, fingerprints, and file state in\n  a per-worker cache and only rebuild when file stats change.\n- API auth checks return missing-auth responses before dynamically importing\n  DB-backed session code.\n- API session caching is TTL-bounded and size-bounded.\n- `buildAuthSessionState()` returns unauthenticated no-cookie state before\n  importing DB-backed session code.\n- DB state is cached on `process` in a path-keyed map so repeated module\n  evaluation reuses the same sqlite client for the same DB path.\n- Home SSR calls `buildRuntimeBootstrap({ includeInitialData: false })`.\n- The root `OmniApp` dynamically imports the heavy `HomeApp` client graph and\n  renders `BootShell` while it loads.\n- The home bootstrap path no longer fetches `/api/agents/catalog` on page load,\n  app unlock, focus, or conversation selection.\n- Catalog requests are reserved for onboarding, Agents settings, and explicit\n  manual refresh. Conversation rendering uses persisted run/worker data and\n  cached/static catalog fallbacks.\n- The catalog API avoids blocking local CLI probes in the frontend request path\n  and returns degraded-but-useful data when live availability is slow.\n\n## Verification Evidence From The Fix\n\nAutomated verification:\n\n- Focused hot-path suite:\n  `tests/api/auth-guard-cache.test.ts`,\n  `tests/api/worker-entries-hot-path.test.ts`,\n  `tests/ui/ssr-bootstrap.test.ts`,\n  `tests/api/conversation-load-coverage.test.ts`,\n  `tests/api/events-route.test.ts`,\n  `tests/api/runtime-bootstrap-route.test.ts`, and\n  `tests/server/workers/output-store.test.ts`.\n- Lifecycle suite: `pnpm test:lifecycle`.\n- ESLint over touched hot-path files.\n\nLive clean-process validation after the fixes:\n\n```text\nNext ready: 3.7s\nInitial / prewarm: 9775ms\nInitial persisted event snapshot prewarm: 5514ms\nInitial worker entries after route compile: 410-445ms\nSteady /: 329-490ms\nSteady /api/auth/session: 398-548ms\nSteady worker entries auth miss: 416-597ms\nsqlite FDs: stable at 4\n```\n\nThe old contaminated process had 34 sqlite-related FDs and request times in the\ntens of seconds to minutes. The clean process after the fix stayed at 4 sqlite\nFDs and returned steady hot-path requests in under a second.\n\n## Permanent Rules\n\n### Rule 1: The Page Shell Must Be Cheap\n\nThe root page may parse route params and produce a minimal shell bootstrap. It\nmust not synchronously load:\n\n- persisted event snapshots,\n- full settings state,\n- worker transcripts,\n- bridge catalogs,\n- supervisor/recovery reconciliation,\n- project memory,\n- external health probes.\n\nIf a future feature needs those, load them through runtime APIs after the shell\nhas been served.\n\n### Rule 2: Snapshots Carry Cursors, Not Large Bodies\n\nEvent snapshots can include compact metadata and cursor hints. They must not\ninline append-only content such as worker transcript bodies. For workers, the\nsnapshot contract is `workerEntrySeqs`; content comes from\n`GET /api/workers/:workerId/entries?afterSeq=N`.\n\n### Rule 3: Hot Reads Must Be Bounded\n\nFor any endpoint that is called during boot, reload, reconnect, polling, or\nstream wake-up:\n\n- read from a bounded cursor, tail, cache, or compact read model;\n- set short timeouts around external dependencies;\n- return degraded but useful responses when optional state is unavailable;\n- never wait on bridge health checks or reconciliation writes.\n\nA 25 second hot-path request is a control-plane failure even if it eventually\nreturns 200.\n\n### Rule 4: Streaming Appends Must Not Reprocess History\n\nWorker stream append cost must scale with the new entries being appended, not\nwith all historical entries in the transcript. Full transcript scans are only\nallowed for:\n\n- first cache seed after process start,\n- detected external file mutation,\n- compaction/expansion/repair,\n- explicit maintenance scripts.\n\nNormal bridge polling and streaming token updates must not parse the whole\nworker file.\n\n### Rule 5: Top-Level Imports Count As Hot-Path Work\n\nIf a route can return before touching the DB, bridge, file system, or a heavy\nmodule graph, its top-level imports must preserve that property. Use dynamic\nimports after cheap gates such as method checks, auth cookie presence, and\nparameter validation.\n\nThis is especially important for:\n\n- auth guards,\n- session bootstrap,\n- worker entries,\n- event snapshots,\n- settings and catalog routes.\n\n### Rule 6: Resource Singletons Must Be Process-Scoped And Keyed\n\nLocal dev can re-evaluate modules. Do not assume a module-level `const client`\nis enough for scarce resources. DB clients, lock managers, and other process\nresources should be cached on `process` or another true process-level owner and\nkeyed by the path/URL they represent.\n\nFor sqlite, watch FD counts during live validation. A healthy dev web process\nshould not accumulate new sqlite FDs as routes are requested.\n\n### Rule 7: Caches Must Be Bounded\n\nEvery process-local cache introduced to protect a hot path needs an explicit\nbound:\n\n- TTL, size, or both;\n- key space with known cardinality;\n- invalidation behavior for writes or external mutation;\n- test coverage for eviction or no-growth behavior.\n\nDo not trade a DB leak for an unbounded memory cache.\n\n### Rule 8: Dev Prewarm Must Not Mask Broken Hot Paths\n\nPrewarm can make the first interactive page nicer, but it is not a correctness\nfix. If prewarm takes tens of seconds or blocks other requests, that is still a\nbug. Use prewarm logs as performance evidence, not as a place to hide slow\nroutes.\n\n### Rule 9: Catalogs Are Demand-Driven Metadata\n\nWorker catalogs, model catalogs, provider availability, CLI health, and project\nfile indexes are not conversation-load prerequisites. They may support chooser\nmenus, onboarding, diagnostics, and settings pages, but the selected\nconversation must render without waiting for them.\n\nDefault cadence:\n\n- do not fetch `/api/agents/catalog` during root page bootstrap, route\n  selection, app unlock, or focus restore;\n- fetch catalog data when the user opens onboarding or Agents settings, or when\n  the user explicitly refreshes runtime availability;\n- use cached or static definitions while a fresh catalog refresh is pending;\n- put short timeouts around live probes and return partial results instead of\n  serializing the request queue behind a hung local CLI;\n- keep project file indexing behind file mention/search intent, not general app\n  load.\n\n### Rule 10: Test The Failure Shape Directly\n\nEvery future change touching boot, snapshots, auth guards, worker streams, or\nresource ownership should include at least one targeted assertion from this\nlist:\n\n- unauthenticated hot path returns before importing DB-backed modules;\n- snapshot payload does not contain worker transcript bodies;\n- worker append cache does not rebuild from disk on every streaming append;\n- incremental worker reads are served from the JSONL tail;\n- DB clients are process/path scoped;\n- page bootstrap calls `includeInitialData: false`;\n- root page does not synchronously import the heavy app graph;\n- conversation load and home bootstrap do not eagerly request\n  `/api/agents/catalog` or project file indexes.\n\n## Review Checklist For Future PRs\n\nUse this checklist before merging any change near the control plane:\n\n- Does this route run on page load, reload, reconnect, SSE wake-up, polling, or\n  worker streaming cadence?\n- What are its top-level imports, and do any of them open DB handles, start\n  schema initialization, read large files, or probe the bridge?\n- Is this request optional metadata such as catalog, model, availability, or\n  file-index data? If so, why is it on the current hot path?\n- Is the worst-case read bounded by a cursor, tail window, limit, or cache?\n- Can it return a degraded response if optional state is slow?\n- Does it include append-only bodies in a broad snapshot?\n- Does it create a process-local cache, and is that cache bounded?\n- Does it create a scarce resource, and is that resource owned by a stable\n  process-level singleton?\n- What command proves it does not regress?\n- What live metric should stay flat: sqlite FDs, RSS, response time, or all\n  three?\n\n## Commands We Used To Diagnose\n\nRun lookup:\n\n```bash\nsqlite3 sqlite.db \"select id,status,mode,title,updated_at from runs where id = '<runId>';\"\nsqlite3 sqlite.db \"select id,run_id,type,status,bridge_session_id,worker_number,updated_at from workers where run_id = '<runId>' order by updated_at desc;\"\nsqlite3 sqlite.db \"select event_type,worker_id,created_at,substr(details,1,200) from execution_events where run_id = '<runId>' order by created_at desc limit 20;\"\n```\n\nProcess and sqlite FD checks:\n\n```bash\nps -axo pid,ppid,rss,pcpu,etime,command | rg 'next-server|scripts/dev|remote-restart' | rg -v rg\nPID=$(lsof -tiTCP:3050 -sTCP:LISTEN | head -n1)\nps -o pid=,rss=,pcpu=,etime=,command= -p \"$PID\"\nlsof -p \"$PID\" 2>/dev/null | rg 'sqlite.db($|-wal|-shm)' | wc -l\n```\n\nBounded live request checks:\n\n```bash\ncurl --max-time 10 -sS -o /tmp/omni-root.out -w 'root status=%{http_code} time=%{time_total}\\n' http://127.0.0.1:3035/\ncurl --max-time 10 -sS -o /tmp/omni-auth.out -w 'auth status=%{http_code} time=%{time_total}\\n' http://127.0.0.1:3035/api/auth/session\ncurl --max-time 10 -sS -o /tmp/omni-worker.out -w 'worker status=%{http_code} time=%{time_total}\\n' 'http://127.0.0.1:3035/api/workers/<workerId>/entries?afterSeq=0'\n```\n\nUse bounded checks. Do not run unbounded stress loops on a machine already\nshowing memory pressure or UI instability.\n\n## Tests That Guard This Class\n\n- `tests/ui/ssr-bootstrap.test.ts` checks that the page bootstrap avoids\n  persisted snapshots, that worker/auth hot paths avoid eager DB imports, and\n  that the heavy `HomeApp` graph is dynamically loaded.\n- `tests/api/worker-entries-hot-path.test.ts` checks that the common\n  run-id-derived worker entries route can serve without importing DB/schema and\n  that missing auth returns before DB-backed work.\n- `tests/api/auth-guard-cache.test.ts` checks that API session validation is\n  reused and bounded.\n- `tests/server/workers/output-store.test.ts` checks tail reads, latest-seq\n  reads, write cache behavior, external file mutation refresh, append/compaction\n  ordering, and crash-truncated lines.\n- `tests/api/events-route.test.ts` checks snapshot shape and event behavior.\n- `tests/app/home-queries-catalog.test.ts` checks that home bootstrap does not\n  eagerly fetch catalog or project file data and only does so for explicit\n  user-facing catalog/file workflows.\n- `pnpm test:lifecycle` checks reconnect, restart, failover, recovery, delete,\n  and process-session behavior over HTTP/SSE.\n\n## Anti-Patterns To Refuse\n\n- \"Just include the entries in the snapshot so the frontend has everything.\"\n- \"This route only imports the DB; it does not query until later.\"\n- \"The full JSONL read is fine because files are small right now.\"\n- \"Prewarm will hide the slow first request.\"\n- \"A process-local cache is small enough without a limit.\"\n- \"Dev-only slowness is acceptable for the control plane.\"\n- \"The worker is running, so a reload can wait.\"\n- \"We need fresh worker availability before showing an existing conversation.\"\n- \"Fetching the catalog on focus is harmless because the response is cached.\"\n\nThe worker may be running for hours. The page still has to serve.\n\n## May 22, 2026 — Recurrence and Fixes\n\nSame class of failure resurfaced after weeks of stability. Symptoms from the\nrunning dev stack:\n\n```text\nGET /api/settings 200 in 47865ms\nPOST /api/agents/prewarm-worker 500 in 86165ms   (bridge ECONNRESET)\nPOST /api/agents/prewarm-worker 500 in 123530ms  (bridge not_found after restart)\nGET /api/workers/<id>/entries?afterSeq=0 200 in 41086ms\n```\n\nOnce one route blocked the event loop, every concurrent request piled up\nbehind it, including auth-rejected calls that never reach a handler.\n\n### Root causes found\n\n1. **`/api/settings` GET ran `canonicalizePersistedProjectRoots` on every\n   poll.** That helper iterates all runs + all workers, does sync\n   `fs.existsSync` per run, and serial `db.update` per drifted row. With a\n   large run history and React Query plus SSE reconnect both polling\n   settings, this saturated the loop for tens of seconds. Canonicalization\n   only matters when `PROJECTS` changes — which only happens on `POST`.\n\n2. **`readEntriesByKey` (in `src/server/workers/output-store.ts`) was an\n   unbounded Map.** Each value is the full parsed transcript for one\n   `(runId, workerId)` chain. A supervisor cycling …7031 tokens truncated…he run has\nsettled; a one-shot best-effort cancel is not sufficient.\n\nAsserting on rendered DOM state is the wrong granularity. We assert on the\nserver's *decisions*, which are now first-class events.\n\n### Rule 7: the test harness runs in isolation\n\nA separate Node process. A temporary `OMNI_HOME`. A fresh sqlite. A dedicated\nport. No collision with the real dev server. Tear it all down on exit.\nScenarios can run in parallel because each one owns its own server.\n\nThis isolation must not trust inherited runner environment. Agents spawned by\nOmniHarness may inherit server control variables, so Vitest always replaces\n`OMNIHARNESS_ROOT` with a newly created temporary root. Database startup in a\nrecognized test process refuses any non-temporary root, and ACP agent children\nmust not receive `OMNIHARNESS_ROOT`, `OMNIHARNESS_INSTANCE`, bridge addresses,\nor runner addresses. A test failure is always preferable to opening live data.\n\n### Rule 8: snapshot bootstrap, event tail thereafter\n\nEvery harness client starts by calling `GET /api/events?snapshot=1` for state\ntruth, then opens the SSE stream with `Last-Event-ID` set to the id at\nsnapshot time. This is the canonical pattern. The UI should do this too;\nright now it doesn't, which is a latent bug.\n\n### Rule 9: snapshots declare scoped completeness\n\nAn event snapshot may be a full replacement for a selected run's transcript,\nor it may be only a partial update. The payload must say which one it is.\n\n`messageScope` carries the contract:\n\n- `runIds`: the conversation run ids whose message set the payload is talking\n  about. For promoted implementation runs this includes the parent planning\n  run plus the selected implementation run.\n- `complete`: `true` means the payload contains the complete message set for\n  those run ids, so absent messages may be removed locally. `false` or a\n  missing scope means the payload is additive and must not erase durable\n  messages already known to the client.\n\nNever infer completeness from \"this snapshot contains a message for that run.\"\nThat was the race behind the disappearing preflight confirmation: a partial\nlive update containing only the user checkpoint looked authoritative enough to\nerase the supervisor confirmation from frontend state.\n\n`snapshotScope` extends the same idea to bounded streams that live in\nartifact storage (execution events, supervisor interventions, planning review\nfindings). Each entry reports `{limit, complete, oldestCreatedAt}`. Clients\nthat want older records keep a cursor (`oldestCreatedAt`) and request a\ndeeper window; clients that just need the head trust the snapshot and stop.\n\n### Append-only artifact streams\n\nThe bulky payload fields of these record families now live in JSONL files\nunder `<projectPath>/.omniharness/run-data/<runId>/`, not in SQLite:\n\n- `execution_events.details` → `execution-events.jsonl`\n- `supervisor_interventions.{prompt,summary}` → `supervisor-interventions.jsonl`\n- `planning_review_findings.{details,recommendation}` → `planning-review-findings.jsonl`\n- `worker_entries` (per-worker) → `workers/<workerId>.jsonl`\n\nThe metadata layer (`artifact_streams`) keeps a row per (runId, kind, ownerId)\nwith `latest_seq`, `latest_record_id`, `compacted_at`, and the resolved\n`project_path` + `relative_root_path`. Each domain row keeps a content hash\nand a short preview so list views don't need to read the artifact. Failure\nmodes surface through named events:\n\n- `artifact.append_failed` — JSONL write or lock acquisition failed.\n- `artifact.metadata_mismatch` — `latest_seq` and the file tail disagree.\n- `artifact.compaction_failed` / `artifact.compaction_completed` — terminal-run\n  sweep result.\n- `artifact.payload_missing` — domain row points at an artifact line that\n  isn't on disk (run `pnpm exec tsx scripts/artifact-repair.ts`).\n- `artifact.backfill_failed` — emitted by the migration script.\n\nSnapshot readers tolerate hydration failures: rows render from the preview\ncolumn and emit `artifact.payload_missing` so an operator can repair.\n\n### Rule 10: `awaiting_user` implies a visible question\n\nA selected run with `status=\"awaiting_user\"` must include a visible supervisor\nmessage with kind `clarification` or `implementation_confirmation`. The\ntransition that creates this state must persist the clarification row, the\nsupervisor message, the run status, and the lifecycle event before notifying\nSSE clients.\n\nIf a snapshot violates this invariant, it surfaces a `Lifecycle` frontend\nerror instead of leaving the UI stuck on \"Loading Omni's question\". The error\nis not a substitute for the invariant; it is the safety rail that makes any\nfuture violation observable.\n\n### Rule 11: terminal user actions retire recovery ownership first\n\nA user stop is not complete when only `runs.status` and `workers.status` are\nterminal. Before publishing the terminal run state, the server synchronously\ncancels volatile and durable wakes, clears wake leases, and resolves every open\nrecovery incident with its normal named event. Otherwise a later sync or timer\nstill owns permission to reactivate the run. Once cancelled, the run rejects\nlate live-worker snapshots from the interrupted turn even when the provider\ncontinues reporting `working` briefly.\n\nConversation deletion follows the same ownership rule. Before deleting a\nworker or run, enumerate and delete every row that references it, including\ncredential allocations and token usage. Route tests must insert a row in each\nworker-referencing table so new foreign keys cannot silently make deletion\npartial or impossible.\n\n### Rule 12: dependent selections cross the boundary together\n\nWorker type, account, model, and effort are one compound composer selection.\nThe value shown in the composer, sent to prewarm, and submitted to conversation\ncreation must come from the same compatibility resolution. A raw account id\nfrom a previously selected worker type is not an explicit preference for the\nnew worker.\n\nRun selection restores the whole compound selection, including the account.\nOptimistic run snapshots must carry the same selection fields as the durable\nrun so selecting a newly created conversation cannot replace an explicit\naccount with `auto` before the authoritative snapshot arrives.\n\nThe server still validates every explicit account selection, but it does so\nbefore creating plan, run, worker, message, or artifact state. Rejections use\nthe original client error status and emit `error.surfaced` with a stable code;\nthey never leave a partially created conversation for snapshots to discover.\n\n---\n\n## Anti-patterns to refuse on sight\n\nThese are the specific shapes of code that produce the bugs in this document.\nReviewers should reject these on sight.\n\n1. **Silent early returns in server methods.**\n   ```ts\n   if (hasLeftoverState) return; // ← BUG\n   ```\n   If a method refuses to proceed, it emits an event explaining why.\n\n2. **try/catch that swallows.**\n   ```ts\n   try { await doThing(); } catch { /* ignore */ } // ← BUG\n   ```\n   Either rethrow, or emit `error.surfaced` with the context. Never both\n   silent and continuing.\n\n3. **Client-side derivation of server decisions.**\n   If the server decided something (plan is ready, recovery gave up), the\n   server emits the event. The client does not re-derive it. If the client\n   is computing `derivePlanningStatus()` from raw fields, that is a missing\n   server event.\n\n4. **SSE frames without `id:`.**\n   Every frame has an id. No exceptions.\n\n5. **State diffs as the primary observability mechanism.**\n   \"The UI will figure out what happened by diffing snapshots\" is not an\n   observability strategy. Name the event.\n\n6. **Fault injection inside production code paths.**\n   `if (process.env.CHAOS) throw new Error(\"boom\")` does not appear in\n   server code. Chaos is a client-side concern.\n\n7. **Tests that boot Chromium to assert on control-plane behaviour.**\n   Use the HTTP/SSE harness. Reserve Playwright for actual UI behaviour\n   (rendering, input handling, layout).\n\n8. **DELETE handlers that don't enumerate dependent rows.**\n   If a row has foreign-key dependents, the DELETE handler either deletes\n   them in a transaction or emits `conversation.delete_failed` with the\n   blocking table/row. Never let the FK error reach the client as a raw 500.\n\n9. **Recovery loops without a terminal state.**\n   If `autoAttemptCount` keeps incrementing without an `abandoned` or\n   `gave_up` terminal event, there is no way for anyone — user, UI, test —\n   to know the system has given up. Always have a terminal state, and\n   always emit it.\n\n10. **Test-only code paths.**\n    `if (process.env.NODE_ENV === \"test\")` in production code is a bug. The\n    test harness should be able to drive production code paths from the\n    outside. The only exception is the dev-only `/api/events/log` polling\n    endpoint, which is build-stripped, has no behavioural effect, and exists\n    purely as a read-side affordance.\n\n---\n\n## How to add a new server-side decision\n\nThe checklist, every time:\n\n1. Pick the event name. Format: `domain.verb` (`worker.spawned`,\n   `plan.review.blocked`). Past tense for things that happened, no\n   \"will/should\".\n2. Define the payload shape in `src/server/events/named-events.ts` (TypeScript\n   union, exported).\n3. At the point of decision, call `emitNamedEvent(\"domain.verb\", payload)`.\n   The emitter writes to the ring buffer and triggers the SSE notifier.\n4. If the decision is a *failure* the user should see, also emit\n   `error.surfaced` with a stable code and human message.\n5. Write a scenario test that asserts the event fires under the expected\n   conditions. If the test cannot assert this, the event is not specific\n   enough — go back to step 1.\n6. The UI may or may not consume the event. That is a separate choice. The\n   event exists regardless.\n\nIf you find yourself unable to complete step 5, the design is wrong, not the\ntest.\n\n---\n\n## How to debug \"the user reports X did not happen\"\n\nThe procedure:\n\n1. Open the event log for the run: `GET /api/events/log?runId=<id>`.\n2. Look for the named event corresponding to X.\n3. If it is present: the server did the thing. The bug is in the UI or in\n   the user's mental model.\n4. If it is absent: the server did not do the thing. Find the code path that\n   *would* have emitted it, and find the early-return / swallowed error /\n   silent branch that prevented it. Fix that, and emit the appropriate event\n   (success or failure).\n5. If the code path doesn't emit anything in either branch: that is the bug.\n   Add the event per \"How to add a new server-side decision.\"\n\nEvery reported bug should land at one of these four answers. If the answer is\n\"I don't know, the server is a black box\", we have failed Rule 1.\n\n---\n\n## Worker conversation content vs. lifecycle events\n\nThese two surfaces are distinct and must stay distinct.\n\n- **Lifecycle events** (`worker.spawned`, `worker.status`,\n  `worker.terminal`, `recovery.*`, etc.) live in the ring buffer and on\n  the SSE stream. They are typed in `src/server/events/named-events.ts`\n  and emitted via `emitNamedEvent`. Their purpose is observability:\n  what decision did the server make.\n- **Worker conversation content** (what the worker said, what tools\n  it called, what the user typed, what the supervisor steered) lives\n  in the unified worker stream — one append-only JSONL per worker. Stop disables future autostart and\npreserves binaries, configuration, logs, and provider credentials.\n\n### Cross-CLI handoff lifecycle\n\nA direct or commit conversation never changes CLI type in place. Ready and launch claims expire; the\nwatchdog either adopts a target found by `runs.origin_handoff_id` or restores the source\nto its durable quota wait / recovery state. Any named event emitted\n*during* the snapshot build — id < marker.id — was then silently dropped\non subsequent drains, because the next drain queried\n`getNamedEventsSince(marker.id, ...)`.\n\nFix: drain once more *before* recording the marker, so the marker's id\nis monotonically ahead of all already-emitted named events. The page still has to serve.\n\n## May 22, 2026 — Recurrence and Fixes\n\nSame class of failure resurfaced after weeks of stability. Symptoms from the\nrunning dev stack:\n\n```text\nGET /api/settings 200 in 47865ms\nPOST /api/agents/prewarm-worker 500 in 86165ms   (bridge ECONNRESET)\nPOST /api/agents/prewarm-worker 500 in 123530ms  (bridge not_found after restart)\nGET /api/workers/<id>/entries?afterSeq=0 200 in 41086ms\n```\n\nOnce one route blocked the event loop, every concurrent request piled up\nbehind it, including auth-rejected calls that never reach a handler.\n\n### Root causes found\n\n1. **`/api/settings` GET ran `canonicalizePersistedProjectRoots` on every\n   poll.** That helper iterates all runs + all workers, does sync\n   `fs.existsSync` per run, and serial `db.update` per drifted row. With a\n   large run history and React Query plus SSE reconnect both polling\n   settings, this saturated the loop for tens of seconds. Canonicalization\n   only matters when `PROJECTS` changes — which only happens on `POST`.\n\n2. **`readEntriesByKey` (in `src/server/workers/output-store.ts`) was an\n   unbounded Map.** Each value is the full parsed transcript for one\n   `(runId, workerId)` chain. A supervisor cycling through many workers\n   kept every transcript ever read resident.\n\n3. **`readWorkerEntriesSinceJsonlTail` did quadratic re-parsing.** Each\n   \"after-seq\" tail call re-read and re-parsed back from end of file\n   looking for the cutoff, growing with transcript size.\n\n4. **`seenIdsByKey` / `fingerprintsByKey` / `nextSeqByKey` / `fileStateByKey`\n   write-side chain caches were also unbounded.** Same shape — one entry\n   per `(runId, workerId)`, only cleared on file deletion. A long-running\n   supervisor that cycles workers but never deletes their files leaks\n   forever. Worst offenders are `seenIdsByKey` (one string per persisted\n   entry id) and `fingerprintsByKey` (one map per id).\n\n### Fixes landed\n\n- `src/runtime/http/routes/settings.ts` — removed the\n  `canonicalizePersistedProjectRoots` call from the GET path. POST still\n  canonicalizes on `PROJECTS` writes, which is the only moment it matters.\n- `src/server/workers/output-store.ts` —\n  - `readEntriesByKey`: LRU-bounded to 32 chains via insertion-order\n    eviction + cache-hit \"touch\" (`setReadEntriesCache` /\n    `touchReadEntriesCache`).\n  - `readWorkerEntriesSinceJsonlTail`: rewritten to read at most 1 MB from\n    the tail in a single `fs.read`, parse once, return the entries past\n    `afterSeq`. Falls back to the legacy backward scan only when the 1 MB\n    window can't prove the cutoff.\n  - Write-side chain caches: LRU-bounded to 64 chains shared across\n    `seenIdsByKey` / `fingerprintsByKey` / `nextSeqByKey` /\n    `fileStateByKey` (`rememberChainKey`). Eviction is safe — the next\n    `refreshChainCaches` call rebuilds from disk + DB-tracked\n    `latestSeq`.\n\n### Tests added\n\n`tests/server/workers/output-store.test.ts` — new `output-store cache\nmemory bounds` block proves the caps hold numerically under simulated\nmulti-worker stress:\n\n- 80 worker chains → `readEntriesByKey.size ≤ 32`\n- 120 worker chains → `seenIdsByKey` / `fingerprintsByKey` /\n  `nextSeqByKey` each `≤ 64`\n- Hot worker stays cached through 100 cold worker churn (no extra disk\n  refreshes after the LRU is full)\n\nThese act as a regression gate: any future commit that re-introduces an\nunbounded cache fails CI.\n\n### Verification under live multi-worker load\n\nAfter restart (dev stack restarted under `nohup`) with all four ACP\nbinaries on PATH (`claude-agent-acp`, `codex-acp`, `gemini`, `opencode`),\nexercised the bridge directly at `:7800` to simulate a supervisor:\n\n```text\n# Concurrent prewarm of all 4 worker types\nclaude:   200 0.15s\ncodex:    200 0.69s\ngemini:   200 14.91s   (gemini-cli's inherent startup, not a regression)\nopencode: 200 16.25s\n\n# Bridge /agents responsiveness during prewarm: 2-7ms\n\n# 3 concurrent claude agents spawned + each handed a real Claude API\n# round-trip via POST /agents/<name>/ask\nspawn-w1: 201 0.14s\nspawn-w2: 201 1.82s\nspawn-w3: 201 1.69s\n\nask-w1:   200 2.15s  → response: \"OK\"\nask-w2:   200 2.18s  → response: \"OK\"\nask-w3:   200 2.38s  → response: \"OK\"\nask wall: 2.40s for all three concurrent\n\n# 10 concurrent /api/settings DURING the ACP message exchanges\nsettings#1..10: 0.93-1.00s each — no degradation\n\n# Bridge RSS during/after: 43-52 MB stable across 10 child subprocesses\n# Web RSS: 1.3 GB stable\n# User's pre-existing workers (gemini+codex) survived undisturbed\n# Zero ECONNRESET, zero timeouts\n```\n\nCompared against the failure baseline:\n\n| Metric                           | Before fix          | After fix + restart |\n| -------------------------------- | ------------------- | ------------------- |\n| Single `/api/settings`           | 47 s (timeout)      | 0.65-0.95 s         |\n| `/api/agents/prewarm-worker`     | 86 s → 500 ECONNRESET | 0.15-16.2 s, all 200 |\n| 30 concurrent `/api/settings`    | (would saturate)    | 1.4 s wall, 1.16-1.32 s each |\n| 10 concurrent settings DURING ACP traffic | (would crash)    | 0.93-1.00 s each    |\n| Bridge memory after prewarm+ask  | crashed/restarted   | 43.4 MB stable      |\n| ECONNRESET under load            | reproducible        | none observed       |\n\n### Anti-patterns added (additive to the list above)\n\n- \"Settings GET is idempotent so we can do fixups inside it.\" — only the\n  fixup is idempotent; the cost is per-call. Fixups belong on the writes\n  that cause drift.\n- \"The chain cache only grows by a few KB per worker.\" — multiplied by a\n  supervisor cycling workers for hours, it is unbounded. Every\n  module-level Map keyed by a per-run-or-worker identifier needs an LRU\n  cap with a regression test, not a \"small enough\" assertion.\n- \"If we evict the dedup cache we'll re-append duplicates.\" — safe iff\n  eviction triggers a disk + DB re-read of the canonical state on the\n  next access. Verify that path exists before claiming the cache is\n  load-bearing.\n\n## August 5, 2026 — Third recurrence, this time on the client\n\nReported symptom: with several sessions streaming at once the UI became slow to\nclick (especially the elicitation/permission forms), slow to scroll, and would\nperiodically freeze outright. Unlike the May incidents, server request times\nwere fine — the damage was on the browser's main thread.\n\n### Root cause: delta wake-ups were still forcing full snapshot rebuilds\n\nThe May fixes correctly moved worker transcript bodies *off* the snapshot\n(Rule 2) and gave clients an incremental content channel: the\n`worker.entry_appended` named event is a wake-up carrying only `(workerId,\nseq)`, and the client pulls from `GET /api/workers/:id/entries?afterSeq=N`.\n\nWhat was never done was decoupling that wake-up from the snapshot rebuild:\n\n1. `writeWorkerOutputEntries` emitted one `worker.entry_appended` **per\n   appended entry** (`output-store.ts`).\n2. `emitNamedEvent` called `notifyEventStreamSubscribers()` unconditionally\n   (`named-events.ts`).\n3. That bumped a **process-global** counter and fired every listener\n   (`live-updates.ts`).\n4. Every parked SSE stream resolved immediately and rebuilt a full payload\n   (~40 SQLite queries, a bridge fetch, and two serializations of a\n   multi-hundred-KB object).\n\nSo the event designed to make snapshots unnecessary was the thing triggering\nthem, at transcript-token cadence, for every connected client. Because the\ncounter is global and unscoped, output on run A rebuilt run B's snapshot too —\ncost scaled as `streaming_workers × connected_clients`.\n\n### Secondary causes found in the same pass\n\n- **Dead payload weight.** `db.select().from(runs)` pulled every column.\n  Measured on a real database: 130 non-archived runs carrying **142,579 bytes\n  of `gitBaselineJson`** in every frame, with zero frontend consumers — the\n  field existed only as a declaration in `shared/home-types.ts`.\n- **Dead change detection.** `EventStreamStateManager.update` guarded with\n  `Object.is(nextState, this.state)` where `nextState` was a freshly allocated\n  literal, so the guard could never fire. Every frame — including re-delivered,\n  byte-identical poll payloads — took a new state identity and re-rendered the\n  shell.\n- **O(runs × messages), three times over.** The sidebar's Active-tab\n  classification rescanned every message, queued message, worker and agent\n  once per run, allocating two `Date` objects per comparison, and did so from\n  three separate places per frame.\n- **Unmemoized transcript.** `MarkdownContent` re-parsed every message on every\n  render with no cache. `terminalUiManager` is one flat store shared by every\n  tool/thought/group in the transcript and broadcasts to all subscribers, so a\n  single disclosure click re-rendered every row — this was the reported click\n  latency. Only two `React.memo` calls existed in the entire codebase.\n- **Layout thrash.** Terminal's pre-paint `useLayoutEffect` did\n  read `scrollHeight` → write `scrollTop` → read `scrollHeight` again, forcing\n  two synchronous layouts per commit.\n- **Storage on the interaction path.** `setElicitationDraft` did a synchronous\n  `sessionStorage.setItem` before the state update that repaints the control.\n\n### Fixes landed\n\n- `live-updates.ts` — `notifyEventStreamSubscribers({ snapshotRelevant })`\n  maintains a second counter. `named-events.ts` classifies\n  `worker.entry_appended` as delta-only.\n- `routes/events.ts` — the SSE park loop drains cheap named frames on every\n  wake but floor-gates rebuilds: 250 ms for snapshot-relevant changes, 2 s for\n  delta-only wakes.\n- `output-store.ts` — one wake-up per append batch carrying the highest seq\n  (safe: `WorkerEntriesManager.onWakeUp` fetches from its own cursor).\n- `events/run-snapshot-fields.ts` — shared column trimming for both snapshot\n  builders. Drops `gitBaselineJson` and `plannerReadinessVerdictJson`\n  outright; scopes `plannerArtifactsJson` to the selected run.\n- `supervisor/observer.ts` — the unconditional per-poll notify moved inside the\n  `claimedTransition` guard.\n- `EventStreamStateManager.ts` — real change detection via the server's\n  `snapshotChecksum`.\n- `sidebar-activity.ts` — `buildSidebarActivityIndex` computes per-run rollups\n  in one pass; classification is now O(workers in run).\n- `MarkdownContent.tsx` — `memo` + `useMemo` around the parse, with the\n  hook-free `renderMarkdownContent` kept exported for the structure tests.\n- `Terminal.tsx` — per-id `useManagerSelector` reads replace five whole-state\n  subscriptions; `ActivityRow` memoized; single pre-write `scrollHeight` read;\n  cached activity fingerprint.\n- `globals.css` / `Terminal.tsx` — `content-visibility: auto` on transcript\n  rows.\n- `component-state-managers.ts` — elicitation draft writes batched off the\n  click path.\n\n### Permanent rules added\n\n#### Rule 11: A Wake-Up Is Not A Rebuild\n\nIf a named event fully describes its own change, emitting it must not force a\nsnapshot rebuild. Classify it delta-only. Snapshot rebuilds are expensive\nenough that they need an explicit floor interval, not \"whenever something\nhappened\".\n\n#### Rule 12: Broadcast Payloads Need Column Projection\n\nAny query whose rows go out on a broadcast channel must select an explicit\ncolumn list, like `WORKER_SNAPSHOT_COLUMNS` already does. `select()` on a table\nwith JSON blob columns ships those blobs to every client on every frame. Before\nadding a field to a broadcast payload, name its consumer.\n\n#### Rule 13: Guards Must Be Able To Fire\n\nAn equality guard against a freshly allocated object is dead code. If a merge\nallocates unconditionally, compare content — a checksum the server already\ncomputes is cheaper than the render cascade it prevents.\n\n#### Rule 14: Shared Flat Stores Need Per-Key Selectors\n\nA `StateManager` keyed by id and read with `useManagerSnapshot` re-renders every\nsubscriber on any key's change. Components that read one entry out of a shared\nmap must use `useManagerSelector` with a per-id selector.\n\n### Anti-patterns added\n\n- \"The event is small, so emitting it per entry is fine.\" — the frame is small;\n  the rebuild it triggers is not. Cost belongs to the wake-up, not the payload.\n- \"We already moved the big data off the snapshot.\" — necessary, not\n  sufficient. Also move the *trigger*.\n- \"The component is cheap to re-render.\" — not when it is rendered once per\n  transcript entry and re-parses markdown each time. Measure per-row cost\n  times row count.\n- \"It's only a sessionStorage write.\" — synchronous storage on a click handler\n  runs before the repaint that acknowledges the click.\n- \"Nothing reads
