```text
    "text": "### Permanent rules added\n\n#### Rule 11: A Wake-Up Is Not A Rebuild\n\nIf a named event fully describes its own change, emitting it must not force a\nsnapshot rebuild. Classify it delta-only. Snapshot rebuilds are expensive\nenough that they need an explicit floor interval, not \"whenever something\nhappened\".\n\n#### Rule 12: Broadcast Payloads Need Column Projection\n\nAny query whose rows go out on a broadcast channel must select an explicit\ncolumn list, like `WORKER_SNAPSHOT_COLUMNS` already does. `select()` on a table\nwith JSON blob columns ships those blobs to every client on every frame. Before\nadding a field to a broadcast payload, name its consumer.\n\n#### Rule 13: Guards Must Be Able To Fire\n\nAn equality guard against a freshly allocated object is dead code. If a merge\nallocates unconditionally, compare content — a checksum the server already\ncomputes is cheaper than the render cascade it prevents.\n\n#### Rule 14: Shared Flat Stores Need Per-Key Selectors\n\nA `StateManager` keyed by id and read with `useManagerSnapshot` re-renders every\nsubscriber on any key's change. Components that read one entry out of a shared\nmap must use `useManagerSelector` with a per-id selector.\n\n### Anti-patterns added\n\n- \"The event is small, so emitting it per entry is fine.\" — the frame is small;\n  the rebuild it triggers is not. Cost belongs to the wake-up, not the payload.\n- \"We already moved the big data off the snapshot.\" — necessary, not\n  sufficient. Also move the *trigger*.\n- \"The component is cheap to re-render.\" — not when it is rendered once per\n  transcript entry and re-parses markdown each time. Measure per-row cost\n  times row count.\n- \"It's only a sessionStorage write.\" — synchronous storage on a click handler\n  runs before the repaint that acknowledges the click.\n- \"Nothing reads this field, but it's harmless to include.\" — 142 KB per frame\n  per client of harmless.\n\n## August 27, 2026 — Mobile Network Transfer Incident\n\nThe browser-to-runner connection transferred 7,057,338 bytes in a 12-second\nsample while one selected conversation was open. The selected snapshot was\n926 KB, uncompressed, and live SSE updates repeated the complete 407-run / 549-\nworker catalog even though only one conversation's live state was changing.\nAt the measured rate this was about 2.1 GB per hour for one client.\n\n### Root causes\n\n1. Selected-run SSE frames reused the complete bootstrap payload. The client\n   already had the full catalog, but every live update resent all runs,\n   workers, sessions, plans, and read markers.\n2. The portable Node HTTP server did not negotiate compression for JSON or\n   SSE, so highly repetitive state crossed the network at its raw JSON size.\n3. Healthy clients still validated snapshots every five seconds, and selected\n   worker/transcript streams polled every two to five seconds despite having\n   resumable SSE wake-ups and content cursors.\n\n### Fix and evidence\n\n- Snapshot bootstrap remains complete and authoritative.\n- Selected-run SSE frames declare `snapshotScope.catalog.complete=false` and\n  carry only the selected run, its workers, session, plan, and read marker.\n  The existing manager merges that slice into the bootstrapped catalog.\n- The full payload checksum stays on the partial frame, so snapshot validation\n  can receive `notModified` without redownloading the catalog.\n- The runtime HTTP server gzip-compresses compressible responses, including\n  SSE with `Z_SYNC_FLUSH` so each live frame remains immediately readable.\n- Healthy snapshot validation moved from 5 seconds to 60 seconds. Worker\n  safety polling is clamped to 30 seconds while active and 60 seconds while\n  idle; SSE wake-ups still fetch new transcript content immediately.\n\nAfter restarting the real runner, the same 12-second selected-conversation\nsample transferred 4,647 wire bytes. The live update was 18.9 KB before gzip,\nand the 937 KB bootstrap used 160 KB on the wire. That is a 99.93% reduction\nin the measured live window.\n\n### Permanent rules added\n\n#### Rule 15: Bootstrap Completeness Does Not Belong In Every Live Frame\n\nBootstrap establishes the complete catalog. A run-scoped live channel should\nsend a scoped partial catalog with an explicit completeness contract and merge\nit by stable ids. Never reuse a complete bootstrap object as a convenient live\nevent payload.\n\n#### Rule 16: Remote Text Transports Must Negotiate Compression\n\nJSON, SSE, JavaScript, CSS, HTML, XML, and SVG served by the portable runner\nmust honor `Accept-Encoding`. Streaming compression must flush at frame\nboundaries and preserve backpressure, cancellation, and reconnect behavior.\n\n#### Rule 17: Resumable Streams Make Polling A Safety Net\n\nWhen SSE provides ids, replay/resync, and cursor wake-ups, polling is not the\nprimary transport. Poll at a low validation cadence and use fast polling only\nafter the stream actually fails.\n# Complete Snapshots Must Not Be Live Frames\n\n**Date:** 2026-08-27\n**Context:** OmniHarness browser-to-runner event transport, especially mobile clients\n**Symptom:** A phone transferred roughly 6 GB after using OmniHarness for a short period. A live 12-second sample transferred 7,057,338 bytes.\n**Root Cause:** The SSE route resent an uncompressed 926 KB complete catalog on selected-conversation updates. The catalog held 407 runs, 549 workers, session summaries, plans, and read markers even though only one selected run was changing. Separate five-second snapshot validation and two-to-five-second worker polling added packet churn despite resumable SSE and worker cursors.\n**Fix:** Keep complete catalog delivery in snapshot bootstrap; project selected-run SSE frames to an explicitly partial catalog; retain the full checksum for cheap `notModified` validation; gzip JSON and SSE with frame flushing; move validation polling to 30–60 second safety intervals.\n**Verification:** The real runner measured 4,647 wire bytes over the same 12-second window after restart, a 99.93% reduction. `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm build:interface:web`, focused HTTP/event/client tests, and `pnpm test:lifecycle` verified compilation, streaming flush behavior, scoped merging, cursor recovery, and lifecycle reconnects.\n**Prevention:** Measure wire bytes, decoded frame sizes, frame cadence, and field-level payload weight before optimizing. Require every run-scoped stream to declare catalog completeness, require compression at the portable HTTP boundary, and treat polling as recovery rather than the normal transport when resumable events exist.\n**Skill/Doc Updates:** Updated `docs/architecture/hot-path-responsiveness-and-resource-leaks.md` with the incident evidence and three permanent transport rules. No shared skill needed changes because the existing control-plane and client/server skills already require scoped completeness, cursors instead of bodies, resumable SSE, and bounded hot paths; the missing rule was project-specific enforcement at the HTTP boundary.\n"
```

```text
Message Type: FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: /root
Sender: /root/network_fix_review
Payload:
Remaining findings:

1. [P1] A complete selected-run validation still retains deleted unselected runs, then advances the checksum — [EventStreamStateManager.ts](/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/interface/home/EventStreamStateManager.ts:154). `mergeScopedCatalog` merges whenever `snapshotRunId` is present, even when `catalog.complete === true`. Therefore, after an unselected run is archived, the validation snapshot omits it but `mergeByKey` restores it from current state; the new complete checksum is then stored, so later polls return `notModified` and the stale run remains indefinitely. The existing test at [event-stream-state-manager.test.ts](/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/tests/app/event-stream-state-manager.test.ts:542) explicitly enshrines this behavior. Complete catalog authority should be determined by `catalog.complete`, not whether a selected run ID is present.

2. [P2] An empty scoped deletion removes the run from state but cannot clear the active selection — [events.ts](/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/runtime/http/routes/events.ts:610), [utils.ts](/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/interface/home/utils.ts:46). The frame is scoped to the missing run and declares `catalog.complete=false`. The state manager removes the run, but `shouldClearMissingSelectedRunFromAuthoritativeSnapshot` requires `catalogComplete === true` and `snapshotRunId !== selectedRunId`; both conditions reject this new deletion frame. A remotely deleted/archived selected conversation can therefore leave the UI pointed at a nonexistent run until the 60-second complete validation. The new tests cover route projection and catalog removal separately, but not this end-to-end selection behavior.

Verification:

- New checksum, empty-slice, gzip-negotiation, and helper tests pass.
- Focused result: 101 passed, 5 skipped, 1 failed.
- The acknowledged pre-existing session-sync test still fails alone at [events-route.test.ts](/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/tests/api/events-route.test.ts:1732); the single-read helper fix did not resolve it.
- `git diff --check` passed.

No files were edited.
```
